vnzh_types: For visa B (B/1 work, tourist) public insurance is not available: B holders are not considered residents under the National Insurance Law. Only visas of type A (A/1 for those entitled under the Law of Return, A/5, A/2, A/4) give resident status and access to a health fund (kupat holim), subject to 183 days of lawful residence and a 'centre of life' in Israel.
policy_requirements: For B/1 the employer must arrange a minimal private policy (usually without chronic and pre-existing conditions) — per the expatfocus review; no official policy requirements for other B visas were found.
public_access: Only with a type A visa and a centre of life in Israel (Bituach Leumi); for a B visa there is no access regardless of length of residence.
children_public: Not verified (children of residents with an A visa are usually insured through the fund, not confirmed by a source).
pitfalls: Pre-existing and chronic conditions are excluded in private policies for B/1; no prices for private insurance in the sources found.
sources: https://www.btl.gov.il/English Homepage/Insurance/An Insured Person Residing Abroad/Pages/asrot.aspx; https://www.expatfocus.com/?p=51116

vnzh_types: Private insurance is needed for digital nomad, non-lucrative (passive income), golden visa/investor, family reunification, self-employed/entrepreneurs, study (list on the Sanitas page; expatinsurance.com: DN and Talent Passport - the same requirements as for NLV). NLV holders have no right to the state system and must maintain a private policy for the entire term of the residence permit (expatinsurance.com, secondary source). The official consulate page could not be obtained (404).
policy_requirements: A policy from an insurer licensed in Spain (DGSFP); full coverage as in the public system; sin copagos (no co-payments), sin carencias (no waiting periods), no deductible; coverage throughout Spain; term of at least 12 months / for the whole permit period; a formal certificate in Spanish with dates; repatriation (Sanitas). Travel insurance, EHIC, Medicare/Tricare are not accepted.
public_access: Convenio especial (voluntary public insurance): requires continuous residence of at least 1 year immediately before the application (sanidad.gob.es), no right to public coverage by another route (certificate of non-exportability of the right from the country of origin). I.e. unavailable for the first residence permit; the first year - private only.
public_cost: EUR 60/month per person under 65, EUR 157/month from 65 (sanidad.gob.es; confirmed by myspainvisa.com, updated 23.09.2026). Does not cover outpatient medicines (100% paid by the patient).
children_public: The convenio is individual: each family member applies separately and pays separately (myspainvisa.com; sanidad.gob.es says nothing about dependants). Free entry for children separately not confirmed.

vnzh_types: A general condition for all Aufenthaltstitel (oesterreich.gv.at): for the entire stay, insurance covering 'alle Risiken' and obliging payments in Austria. Acceptable: mandatory insurance through work, voluntary Austrian social insurance with immediate coverage, or private insurance equivalent to the statutory one. Tourist insurance is not suitable. A special residence permit for a digital nomad/passive income was not found on workinaustria.com (described are the Aufenthaltsbewilligung for the self-employed on a temporary basis and the Niederlassungsbewilligung for the self-employed); the Rot-Weiss-Rot Karte for employment - insurance through the employer (ASVG) - was not examined in the sources.
policy_requirements: 'Alle Risiken' and Leistungspflicht in Austria, equivalence to statutory coverage; immediate start of coverage. Travel insurance is not accepted.
public_access: Through employment (ASVG) - immediately. Otherwise Selbstversicherung: 'Personen, die nicht krankenversichert sind und deren Wohnsitz in Österreich liegt, können sich selbst versichern' (oesterreich.gv.at). Waiting period not verified.

children_public: With mandatory insurance of a parent (through work), children are co-insured free of charge (durchblicker.at); children are co-insured without contribution up to 18 (up to 27 if studying) — oesterreich.gv.at; applicability to Selbstversicherung (§ 16 ASVG) not confirmed.

vnzh_types: For the residence permit, proof of health insurance in Poland is required: contributions to ZUS/NFZ (contract + proof of payment), insurance through the employer, foreign insurance (sworn translation) or a private policy. Spouses of Polish citizens and others are exempt.

public_access: Via ZUS when working/in business or voluntary NFZ insurance (available during a break in compulsory insurance; for a break of more than 3 months — a surcharge).
public_cost: Voluntary NFZ in Q2 2026: 835.04 PLN per month (~10,020 PLN/year ~ 2,606 USD); the contribution is revised quarterly; with a break of 3 months to a year — a one-time surcharge of 1,855.64 PLN, more thereafter.
children_public: Per the NFZ document: family members without mandatory coverage are added with no additional contribution (one contribution per family).

vnzh_types: Short-term ikamet (turistik, real-estate, family and others): valid health insurance for the whole term of the permit is mandatory at issuance and extension (Göç İdaresi, circular 2016/16). Enrolment in GSS/SGK is possible after more than 1 year of continuous residence on ikamet (art. 60/1-d of law 5510) and happens on application (SGK/Göç İdaresi brochure); for a family with ikamet since 2022 the condition is met. There is no separate requirement by type of residence permit (real estate vs family) in the sources found. There is no official confirmation whether children under 18 are exempt from the insurance requirement for ikamet - not verified.
policy_requirements: A policy from an insurance company licensed in Turkey (or the Turkish branch of a foreign one), term not shorter than the permit (usually 1 year), with a reference to circular 2016/16 in the text. Minimum limits: outpatient 15,000 TRY/year (deductible 0-40% by type of institution), inpatient 150,000 TRY (out of network, 20% co-participation) - 250,000 TRY (public institutions) or no limit in the contracted network. Emergency treatment and acute illnesses cannot be excluded. The waiting period applies only to the first contract, not on auto-renewal. Exception: a policy from a foreign insurer is acceptable when applying abroad if it meets the minimum limits.
public_access: GSS/SGK under art. 60/1-d of Law 5510: entry on application after more than 1 year of continuous residence on ikamet (official brochure of Göç İdaresi/SGK). For a family with ikamet since 2022 the condition is met, GSS is available now. In the first year of residence insurance for ikamet is private only. The income test is not applied to foreigners (data on application not found).
public_cost: GSS for a foreigner under 60/1-(d): 7,927.20 TRY/month per adult (2026; = 24% of the minimum wage 33,030) - confirmed by turmob.org.tr and ismmmo.org.tr; Feather's figure of 800-1 000 TRY is wrong/outdated. Enrolment - after >1 year of continuous residence.

public_access: The right to Kela and municipal healthcare depends on recognition of permanent residence in Finland or work. Kela: when moving for a year or more one must notify the DVV (obtaining a municipality of residence / kotikunta); if a Migri residence permit is needed, it must be obtained before the right to Kela payments. With a kotikunta there is a right to all necessary public healthcare (client fees). The exact term (for example, a residence permit for 1 year or more) is not explicitly formulated in the official texts found. Work with income from 800.02 EUR/month gives some benefits from day one.
public_cost: There is no separate voluntary contribution: public medicine is funded by taxes, the patient pays client fees; the size of the tax part (sairaanvakuutusmaksu) was not verified.
children_public: Children under 18 in the same household are family members; Kela eligibility is determined by the same recognition of permanent residence of the custodial parent (Kela). Whether it is paid for children is not stated on the pages.

opt_public_formula: A health contribution is not levied on entrepreneurs by law: the contributions law (art. 2) names only pension and unemployment; compulsory health insurance is financed from the budget (art. 57 of the health insurance law); since 2022 the 10.8 % payroll contribution has been abolished. Calculation at $80,000 = $0. Pension 10 % and unemployment 1 % — separately, the base is 150 % of the average salary at a turnover above EUR 15,000 (2026 not calculated).

vnzh_types: Long-term visa / long-term pobyt (more than 90 days): an adult third-country national not participating in public insurance must have commercial 'comprehensive' insurance (komplexní zdravotní pojištění cizinců) for the entire term. Exceptions: employees of Czech employers (public insurance), holders of permanent residence. Since 01.01.2024 minors with a long-term residence permit are necessarily included in public insurance (VZP), a private policy for children is no longer taken out.
policy_requirements: Minimum limit per insured event 400,000 EUR, with no deductible (per Grant Thornton of 20.09.2023 and Charles University guidance of 04.01.2024); policy from a Czech insurer authorized for this type of insurance (after 20.09.2023 the PVZP monopoly was lifted: PVZP, Slavia, UNIQA, AXA, Maxima, SV). The former page of the Czech MFA (Brussels) describes the old 2021 rules (PVZP only) and is outdated. The page of the Czech Interior Ministry's migration service did not open - check on the official site.
public_access: Children under 18 with a long-term residence permit: automatically in public insurance for the term of the residence permit, the policyholder is the legal representative (VZP). Adults: mandatory with permanent residence or when working for a Czech employer; no voluntary entry for adults with a residence permit found in the sources. The time to obtain permanent residence (usually 5 years of continuous residence permit) was not verified in the sources.
public_cost: Each of the two children (the younger child (13), the older child (17)): 3,024 CZK/month from 01.01.2026 (13.5% of the minimum wage of 22,400 CZK; 2025: 2,808; 2024: 2,552) = 36,288 CZK/year per child, 72,576 CZK for two. Paid by the legal representative (VZP). When the older child turns 18, the older child moves to commercial KZPC.
children_public: Minors (under 18) with a long-term residence permit - public insurance is mandatory, but NOT free: 3,024 CZK/month per child in 2026 (paid by the legal representative, vzp.cz, checked 05.10.2026). Both children (the older child (17), the younger child (13)) - in VZP; commercial KZPC is needed only for the sample adult. When the older child turns 18, the child (18 years old) no longer qualifies for public insurance - a commercial policy is needed.
calc_note: Total for three (recalculated 07.10.2026 for the sample household (one adult aged 40, two children aged 17 and 13)) = one sample adult on a commercial KZPC policy + two children on the mandatory VZP state contribution. min = 15,574 + 2 x 12 x 3,024 = 15,574 + 72,576 = 88,150 CZK (was: 2 adults KZPC + 1 child = 67,436 CZK with a child of 19). When the older child turns 18, the older child moves to KZPC: the sum is again 2 x 15,574 + 36,288 = 67,436 CZK. The price per adult is the same with no breakdown by age (the pages have no age scale); the PVZP price is from March 2026, not re-verified. typical (Slavia 2024) is not used.
pitfalls: From 01.01.2024 minors with a long-term residence permit must be in VZP (not free), a private policy is not issued for them.; KZPC: limit >= 400,000 EUR, no spoluúčast; the policy only from a Czech insurer; the PVZP monopoly was lifted on 20.09.2023 (PVZP, Slavia, UNIQA, AXA, Maxima, SV).; KZPC covers necessary/urgent care, not 'premium clinics' - do not count on Na Homolce/Canadian Medical Care without written confirmation.; PVZP prices are not tied to age on the page found; for a 40-year-old the real price may be higher than CZK 15,574.

vnzh_types: Basic insurance (LAMal/KVG) is mandatory for anyone residing in Switzerland, within 3 months after moving (BAG); for a residence permit, insurance is confirmed at registration.
policy_requirements: Each family member, including a child, is insured separately; the insurer may not refuse or introduce a waiting period for basic coverage regardless of age and health; if registered within 3 months, coverage and premiums run retroactively from the date of arrival. Deductible from 300 to 2,500 CHF, co-payment 10%.
public_access: There is no public system, there is mandatory regulated private insurance with licensed insurers (premiums by canton; calculator priminfo.admin.ch). After 3 months the insurer is assigned by the canton.
children_public: Children are insured under a separate policy within 3 months, children's contributions are lower; specific amounts not verified.
calc_note: Average adult price 2026 — 429 CHF/month (~5,148 CHF/year ~ 6,179 USD); by canton from ~317 CHF (Zug) to ~562 CHF (Geneva). Prices for a young adult and a child not found — the total for three is not calculated.
pitfalls: The basic policy does not cover dental, optical, alternative medicine; supplementary policies are separate (Feather International from 80.50 EUR/month). A penalty surcharge for registering later than 3 months.

vnzh_types: Health insurance is mandatory only for study and exchange visas; not required for work, critical skills and business visas (a medical and radiology report is needed). For the retiree visa the regulations and the Home Affairs website contradict each other.

vnzh_types: Not insurance for the visa, but mandatory enrolment in the state NHIS after 6 months of residence regardless of visa type and income (koreabridge, a retelling of the law; the official NHIS page for foreigners did not open).
public_access: NHIS is mandatory for foreigners after 6 months of residence; employees are enrolled through the employer earlier.
public_cost: For employees: total contribution 7.19% of salary (2026), split equally with the employer (~3.6% from the employee). For self-employed/freelancers (local subscribers): a formula based on income, property and car; community estimate 140,000-160,000 KRW per month (~103-118 USD at the rate of 1,353.36) — unofficial.
children_public: Employees can enrol a spouse and children as dependants without separate contributions if the dependant's income is up to 20 million KRW per year and assets are within the threshold.
calc_note: Range 140-160 thousand KRW taken with a midpoint of 150,000; not official. Not calculated for three.
pitfalls: Dentistry and optics are partially covered; the sample adult as a remote worker without Korean income will fall into "local subscribers" with a minimum assessment.

vnzh_types: Foreigners with a residence permit of more than 3 months must join National Health Insurance (Kokumin Kenko Hoken) at the municipality if they have no employer insurance; enrolment is not automatic.
policy_requirements: Private insurance does not replace mandatory NHI; condition — notification of the move and registration of residence.
public_access: Immediately after residence registration for stays over 3 months; refusal risks retroactive payments. The LDP party proposes mandatory prepayment of contributions by foreigners (a proposal, not law).
public_cost: The contribution is calculated per household and depends on last year's income and the municipality; amounts not found.
children_public: Children are part of the household's NHI; the co-payment for children is 20% (for schoolchildren and adults up to 69 — 30%). For ages 40-64 a nursing care contribution is added.
calc_note: Prices not found: the contribution depends on the previous year's income and municipality.
pitfalls: With no Japanese income the contribution is calculated on the minimum base, specifics depend on the city (not verified).
